newsitem.title: ITALY: Enel says ready for sale,up to Italy govt.
newsitem.headline: Enel says ready for sale,up to Italy govt.

text.p: Italian state electricity giant Enel is ready for privatisation and only awaits a government decision, chairman Chicco Testa said.
Testa told reporters attending an international conference here: "We are ready, the prospectus is ready, now it is up to the government to create the authority and then the Treasury."
The planned privatisation of Enel was interrupted last year when it was already well advanced.
Testa said that, in view of the flotation, it was necessary to also envisage "a complete restructuring of the electicity system in order to give investors more security."
The Court of Accounts said on Monday that uncertainty and controversy over electricity tariffs were likely to weigh on the future privatisation of Enel.
Testa said he agreed with the opinion of the court, which oversees state accounts and said that "certainty about tariffs is one of the conditions of privatisation."
He added that the correct tariff mechanism to adopt was that of the so-called price-cap.
According to a government decree law passed in July it will be up to an energy sector authority yet to be created to fix electricity tariffs by June 30, 1997.

A Senate, upper house, industry committee held up approval of the regulatory authority for the energy sector in July. Creation of the authority is vital for the planned privatisation of Enel now expected to start in spring next year.
